question: How is request/command validation implemented in the Resources and ManagementGroups modules? Report: whether FluentValidation or another validator library is used (csproj reference file:line), where validators live (file paths), one example validator with an integer range rule if any exists (file:line excerpt), how a validation failure is turned into an HTTP response (status code, body shape - file:line), and the domain exception types available in Resources (file names). Also report how a Create factory in an existing entity rejects invalid input (exception type, file:line).
claim: No validator library (FluentValidation or otherwise) is referenced anywhere in the backend csproj files searched (Resources.Api, Resources.Core, Shared.Infrastructure, Shared.Abstractions all lack such a reference; a repo-wide search for 'FluentValidation' under backend/ returned no matches). Instead, both the Resources and ManagementGroups modules validate inline inside their MediatR-style command/query handlers (e.g. CreateResourceInstanceCommandHandler.cs, CreateResourceTypeCommandHandler.cs, UpdateManagementGroupCommandHandler.cs) using manual `if`/guard checks that throw module-specific CustomException subtypes (ResourcesDomainException / ManagementGroupsDomainException) — there is no separate 'Validator' class or folder in either module. The single exception is one DataAnnotations use: AddGroupMemberCommandHandler.cs uses `EmailAddressAttribute` (System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations) to check email format. An integer range rule exists as a `Math.Clamp` (not a rejecting validator) on the pagination 'take' parameter in GetResourceInstancesQueryHandler.cs — MinTake=1, MaxTake=50, DefaultTake=20, clamped rather than throwing on out-of-range input. A validation/domain failure becomes an HTTP response via ErrorHandlerMiddleware.cs, which catches all exceptions, resolves them through IExceptionCompositionRoot -> IExceptionToResponseMapper (module-specific mapper first, falling back to the shared default ExceptionToResponseMapper.cs), and writes `context.Response.StatusCode` + `WriteAsJsonAsync(response)`. The shared default mapper maps: NotFoundException -> 404, ForbiddenException -> 403, any other CustomException (including ResourcesDomainException/ManagementGroupsDomainException) -> 400 BadRequest, with body shape `{ Errors: [ { Code, Message } ] }` (record ErrorsResponse(params Error[] Errors), Error(Code, Message)). Resources also has a module-specific mapper (ResourcesExceptionToResponseMapper.cs) that maps ResourceTypeNameAlreadyExistsException to 409 Conflict with body `{ code = "RESOURCE_TYPE_NAME_TAKEN", message }`. Domain exception types present in Resources (by file name, folder backend/src/Modules/Resources/ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.Core/Exceptions/): ResourcesDomainException.cs, ResourcesForbiddenException.cs, ResourcesExceptionToResponseMapper.cs, ResourceTypeNameAlreadyExistsException.cs (no NotFoundException-derived type exists for Resources per core-surface.json and per file listing). Regarding the Create factory: the Create factories themselves (e.g. ResourceType.Create, ResourcePropertyDefinition.Create, ResourceInstance.Create) contain NO validation/guard logic — they are simple object initializers with no throw statements. Rejection of invalid input happens earlier, in the calling command handler, before Create is invoked, via `throw new ResourcesDomainException(...)` (e.g. CreateResourceInstanceCommandHandler.cs:38 'Instance name cannot be empty.' before ResourceInstance.Create is called at line 68; CreateResourceTypeCommandHandler.cs:30 similar for resource type name).
